tested_scope_delta.verified_tool_calls_scope: medium-fault LLM-agent tool-use ablation comparing retry-only, verification-only and verify-before-retry; the reported evidence is a three-cell partial verification/recovery interaction and separately includes up-to-five retries of rate-limited LLM-client responses outside the agent-visible tool retry budget
tested_scope_delta.aid_guard_reference_scope: external-effect recovery admissibility under declared provider contracts using stable predecessor delivery identity, terminalization linearized against effect commit, authoritative terminal lookup, recovery-horizon retention and one-successor authorization only after provider-enforced terminal evidence
tested_scope_delta.overlap: Both mechanisms constrain retry/recovery around uncertain effects and both make hidden retry or duplicate-effect behavior material to correctness.
tested_scope_delta.composition: AID-Guard supplies a lower-layer provider/runtime admissibility substrate that can make a retry or replacement safe and well-defined; Verified Tool Calls supplies an upper-layer verification/retry policy interaction and exposes retry-topology confounds. A clean four-cell experiment can therefore hold the AID-Guard-style provider substrate invariant while toggling lifecycle verification/gating and whether an otherwise admissible recovery action is attempted.
tested_scope_delta.separation: Verified Tool Calls does not provide provider terminalization, authoritative no-effect certification, recovery-horizon fencing or one-successor lineage transfer, and its three-cell ablation lacks verification-OFF/recovery-OFF. AID-Guard does not measure the retry-only versus verification-only versus combined task-performance interaction and does not enumerate the agent/SDK/client retry-policy effect measured by Verified Tool Calls. Neither tested scope contains the other.

finding.hidden_retry_locus_effect: The LLM-client retry loop in Verified Tool Calls strengthens, rather than duplicates, the AID-Guard distinction: a nominal recovery-OFF arm can still contain physical retry unless every retry locus is counted or disabled. Provider-level admissibility and experiment-level retry topology must therefore be modeled separately.
finding.reason: Collapsing Verified Tool Calls into AID-Guard would lose the verification/retry interaction and retry-locus evidence; collapsing AID-Guard into Verified Tool Calls would lose provider-contract recovery admissibility and terminal lineage fencing. The strongest relation is composition across layers, not duplication.
